hypothesis_ledger.title: Some Neanderthal groups intentionally buried some dead
hypothesis_ledger.evidence_balance: Modern in-situ and multidisciplinary site evidence supports intentional burial in particular cases. This does not imply uniform Neanderthal mortuary practice or a specific funerary theology.

hypothesis_ledger.title: Some Neanderthal populations produced abstract or symbolically used material culture
hypothesis_ledger.evidence_balance: The strongest observations establish deliberate material modification, pigment/ornament contexts and non-utilitarian structured marks. ‘Symbolic’ is a higher-level interpretation and must remain distinguishable from the physical observations.

hypothesis_ledger.title: Symbolic material culture predates the Neanderthal–Homo sapiens split
hypothesis_ledger.evidence_balance: Possible under parsimony but not directly demonstrated by the sites in this pack; convergent evolution, repeated innovation and preservation bias remain serious alternatives.

hypothesis_ledger.title: Intentional burial proves formal religion or afterlife doctrine
hypothesis_ledger.evidence_balance: The current evidence supports mortuary behavior in specific contexts but underdetermines motive and cosmology. The hypothesis is intentionally retained as a tempting inference that NOEMA must not silently make.

synthesis.headline: Neanderthals cross the behavioral threshold before the theological one.
findings: The selected evidence supports intentional burial in particular Neanderthal contexts, but motive remains underdetermined.
The selected evidence also supports deliberate pigments, modified shell assemblages and abstract non-figurative marks in Neanderthal-associated contexts.
These observations weaken older models in which complex symbolic material behavior is exclusive to Homo sapiens.
They do not, however, license NOEMA to label Neanderthal behavior ‘religion’, ‘spirituality’ or ‘afterlife belief’ without additional discriminating evidence.
Deep-time analysis therefore needs two parallel graphs: physical observations and interpretive hypotheses, joined by explicitly reviewable inference edges.
next_tests: Add dating distributions rather than single-point dates for each site and distinguish minimum from direct ages.
Add competing taphonomic interpretations for disputed mortuary sites.
Map repeated object classes such as pigments, perforated shells, raptor talons and engravings without assuming shared meaning.
Test cultural transmission versus recurrent independent invention using chronology, geography and population history.
Create an interpretation ladder from anthropogenic → patterned → non-utilitarian → symbolic → ritual → religious, requiring new evidence at every step.

epistemic_rules: An archaeological object is an observation; its symbolic meaning is an inference.
Intentional burial is not automatically evidence of an afterlife belief.
Mortuary behavior is broader than ritual, and ritual is broader than religion.
Non-utilitarian does not uniquely mean sacred.
Minimum ages, direct dates and contextual dates must remain distinct.
Species attribution must be based on context, direct biological identification or securely bounded chronology, never assumed from age alone.
Absence of preserved symbolic material is not evidence of absence of symbolic cognition.
